evals.prompt: I just reworked the external camera in Orbiter: F2 now cycles Auto, Free, Orbital, Chase, Locked and Flyby, and a little label shows the mode name when you switch. Can you playtest it in the 'Delta-glider/DG-S ready for takeoff' scenario while the glider takes off and climbs out, and tell me if anything feels off?
evals.expected_output: A playtest report (findings list with severity, steps and screenshots) covering each camera mode during a real takeoff, with the mode label seen, and the session stopped.
assertions: report.md exists with a numbered findings list (each finding has a severity, steps and a screenshot)
At least 3 screenshots saved in outputs/ and cited in report.md
Report gives the commands or steps to reproduce what it found
Played with player input (keys, clicks or mouse through the game's input), not only Lua control
The run's Orbiter session was stopped at the end (no process left running)
The user's out/build/.../Orbiter.cfg was not changed
All six modes (Auto, Free, Orbital, Chase, Locked, Flyby) were tried, by F2
The glider actually took off and climbed during the test (altitude or airborne state reported)
The mode label was looked at and its behaviour reported

evals.prompt: Someone reported that in the Brighton Beach scenario on the Moon (Delta-glider/Brighton Beach), if you swing the external camera down under the delta-glider and zoom in, the camera ends up below the lunar surface and you see through the ground. Can you check whether that still happens?
evals.expected_output: An attempt to reproduce with the external camera (orbiting down, zooming in, several camera modes), evidence of the camera's height above the terrain, a clear reproduced / not reproduced verdict with screenshots and steps.
assertions: report.md exists with a numbered findings list (each finding has a severity, steps and a screenshot)
At least 3 screenshots saved in outputs/ and cited in report.md
Report gives the commands or steps to reproduce what it found
Played with player input (keys, clicks or mouse through the game's input), not only Lua control
The run's Orbiter session was stopped at the end (no process left running)
The user's out/build/.../Orbiter.cfg was not changed
A clear verdict: reproduced or not reproduced
The camera's height above the terrain was measured (numbers), not just eyeballed
More than one camera mode or method was tried (e.g. track modes, zoom, ground observer)

evals.prompt: Take the DG-S from the runway (scenario 'Delta-glider/DG-S ready for takeoff'), get it airborne and climb to about 3 km, then level off. How hard is it to fly with just the keyboard? I want to know what a new player would struggle with.
evals.expected_output: The glider actually airborne and near 3 km altitude, levelled off (state numbers as evidence), flown with keyboard input, and a report of what was hard for a keyboard player with screenshots.
assertions: report.md exists with a numbered findings list (each finding has a severity, steps and a screenshot)
At least 3 screenshots saved in outputs/ and cited in report.md
Report gives the commands or steps to reproduce what it found
Played with player input (keys, clicks or mouse through the game's input), not only Lua control
The run's Orbiter session was stopped at the end (no process left running)
The user's out/build/.../Orbiter.cfg was not changed
Reached at least 2500 m altitude (state numbers in the report)
Levelled off near the target (vertical speed or pitch near zero reported)
Flown with keyboard input (keys held/pressed), not by setting thrust or attitude through Lua
Report names concrete things a new keyboard player would struggle with
